routes.description: Build a cumulative historical inference from early apostolic provenance, source trustworthiness, reported encounter characteristics, and comparative elimination of alternatives.
routes.successCriteria: The resurrection route succeeds if the selected evidence grounds the reports near the original apostles and makes resurrection a better explanation than legend, sincere error, or deception.

motionBridge.description: The cumulative historical evidence must make resurrection the best explanation of the reported events despite its low prior probability.

centralBridges.description: The resurrection proclamation must be connected to early apostolic sources rather than explained as a later legend.
The documentary sources must possess enough independently supported trustworthiness to carry claims about the resurrection encounters.
Legend, sincere perceptual error, and deliberate deception must be comparatively weakened by the reported evidence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: The cumulative evidence must be capable in principle of overcoming the resurrection hypothesis's acknowledged low prior probability.

routes.description: Show that indirect and untestable Christian reports do not establish the underlying events and cannot discriminate resurrection from ordinary testimonial and literary alternatives.
routes.successCriteria: The skeptical route succeeds if source limitations, live natural alternatives, and the extraordinary causal burden leave the resurrection insufficiently established by the surviving reports.

motionBridge.description: The surviving reports must fail to provide sufficiently testable and causally discriminating support for a historical resurrection.

centralBridges.description: The documentary record must remain too anonymous, indirect, inconsistent, or inaccessible to establish the claimed events strongly.
The explanatory framing must not assume the historicity of events that could instead reflect legendary development.
The evidential method must not warrant resurrection when comparable standards would admit rejected extraordinary claims or more probable ordinary errors.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Sincerity, transformation, or willingness to suffer must remain compatible with sincerely held false beliefs.

sections.title: Early Apostolic Provenance and Testability
sections.rationale: Whether the resurrection claim reaches identifiable original apostles determines whether the surviving documents provide direct historical grounding or inaccessible hearsay.

sections.title: Legend and the Explanatory Starting Point
sections.rationale: The inference depends on whether legend is adequately included as an alternative or whether the framework prematurely assumes events requiring explanation.

sections.title: Documentary Trustworthiness and Ordinary Corroboration
sections.rationale: The historical burden turns on whether confirmations of ordinary details warrant trust in extraordinary claims or remain compatible with dependence and error.

sections.title: Sincerity, Martyrdom, and Honest Error
sections.rationale: The parties dispute whether costly commitment and transformed conduct reduce deception and mistake or merely demonstrate sincere belief.

sections.title: Prior Probability and Extraordinary Evidence
sections.rationale: The motion requires determining whether cumulative documentary evidence can overcome a low miracle prior or whether ordinary error remains more probable.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Four exhaustive explanatory categories frame the case: later myth, sincere mistake, deliberate deception, or an actual resurrection.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Paul's early resurrection tradition and agreement with Peter, James, and the Twelve place the resurrection claim with the original apostles.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: The apostles' willingness to suffer and die, along with the transformations of James and Peter, counts against deliberate fabrication and favors resurrection as the explanation.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: A miraculous claim properly receives a low prior probability, but sufficiently strong cumulative documentary evidence can overcome even an extremely small prior.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Numerous historical confirmations and undesigned interconnections among the Gospels and Acts cumulatively support their substantial trustworthiness and informed proximity to events.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: The biblical reports lack secure custody, sworn or examinable testimony, known provenance, and physical corroboration, so their resurrection claims cannot be adequately tested.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: The proposed explanatory alternatives begin too far downstream by assuming the reported death and resurrection events, while overlooking legendary development of the story.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Legend means the reported events themselves may be unwarranted, and sincere belief or martyrdom cannot validate them because equally sincere false beliefs are widespread.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: Shared or compatible mundane details may arise through common stories or literary dependence and do not validate extraordinary resurrection assertions.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-08.proposition: A natural alien-visitation hypothesis is more antecedently plausible than a violation of known natural regularities, while no resurrection has been independently and scientifically verified.
